title: Weaver Ants Sew Leaves Together Using Their Own Babies

scenes.text: These ants sew leaves together using their own babies.
A worker holds a larva in its jaws and taps its head with its antennae.
The larva releases silk, and the worker drags the thread from leaf to leaf.
If the leaves are too far apart, the ants grab each other and form a living chain.
Some colonies top 500,000 ants. One mapped colony spanned 17 trees.
Their sewing machine is a baby.
scenes.keywords: ants weaving leaf nest close up

description:
These ants sew leaves together using their own babies.
Weaver ants squeeze silk from their larvae to stitch leaves into nests the size of a soccer ball, and form living chains to pull leaves closer. Some colonies top 500,000 ants.
Would you trust a baby with a sewing job? Comment below.
first_comment: Living chains of ants pull leaves together. Which animal is the best builder you know?
